messages.subject: fitting models to ARGOS data
parts:
Hi Dr. Fleming et al.,
I'm a MS student interested in using the ctmm package to analyze winter home ranges for a species of heron. The data was collected using the ARGOS system, and I am wondering if there is a way to incorporate the error associated with different location classes (3, 2, 1, 0) into the models. When I fit models including all location classes, the variograms do not reach an asymptote. So, I have attempted to fit the models by filtering the dataset to include only the most accurate points (location class 3, < 250 meters), but this reduces my sample sizes significantly in some cases and am still not getting good fits. I am not sure why this is. I've included plots for one individual. Thanks in advance for any insight.

> summary(fitted.mods.61)
                   dAICc DOF[mean]
OU anisotropic  0.000000  113.9902
OUF anisotropic 2.100069  114.0238
IID anisotropic 2.611538  124.0000


Kristie

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: fitting models to ARGOS data
parts:
Hi Kristie,

I'm assuming this is daily data from the variogram plots. I suppose 250 meter error would be substantial on that plot as (250 m)^2 = 6.25 hm^2.
[If the data are sampled irregularly, you can also try fast=FALSE in variogram() to reduce smoothing bias on the empirical variogram, which can look like autocorrelation.]

There is some literature on the estimated error radii of ARGOS error classes. E.g.: http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/wol1/doi/10.1111/j.1748-7692.2002.tb01025.x/abstract
For the time being you could translate those results into a GPS-like HERE data column, which is sqrt(var(x)+var(y)) IIRC, and then set error=TRUE in the model before fitting.
I'm going to be doing this in a couple of months though, to where it will import automatically. I have one last project on my plate before I will be heading a big paper on telemetry errors.

Best,
Chris

parts:
Hi Chris,

Thanks for your advice on this. The tags are transmitting for four hours every other day resulting in irregular data based off of when satellites are available, so I've added fast = FALSE into the variogram() function. I've also tried adding the error information into the dataset using the published ARGOS error classes (250 m for LC 3 and 500 m for LC 2). However, from the resulting plot (plot 1), it is not correctly incorporating the error. Is it incorrect to use the error values published by ARGOS in the UERE column? Or is the resulting plot because the model is not robust to high amounts of error in this example? I'm happy to send this example if it would be useful. Thanks so much for your time. I'm very much looking forward to your publication on the matter.

Plot 1. akde(x, error = TRUE)
Plot 2. does not incorporate error


Kristie

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: fitting models to ARGOS data
parts:
Hi Kristie,

That's not the error option that you want. error in akde is for capping the numerical errors caused by kernel truncation.

There is a short section on activating telemetry errors in the variogram vignette. This will be updated to its own longer vignette soon.
In short, you have to turn on errors in the model guess/prototype, prior to the final model fit.

You can feel free to email/message a copy of your data to me. I'm working on the errors paper right now and I need some ARGOS data of your type (with the error categories) to test as.telemetry and ctmm.fit on.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: fitting models to ARGOS data
parts:
Hi Kristie,

The master branch on GitHub can now import ARGOS error information and will automatically convert your location classes to error ellipses using calibration results from Vincent et al (2002), which were the best I could find in the literature.

However, I haven't yet updated the Kalman filter to handle error ellipses and so, at the moment, only the error circles are being used, which is not ideal for ARGOS data, as you probably know.

Here's what I am getting so far, but I wouldn't trust the spread of the range yet until the error ellipses are supported:

CSV <- read.csv("../DATA/Kristie Stein/ctmm.heron61.csv")
# north preserving projection to check against longitudinal error/spread
proj <- paste("+proj=aeqd +lon_0=",median(CSV$location.long)," +lat_0=",median(CSV$location.lat)," +datum=WGS84",sep="")
DATA <- as.telemetry(CSV,timeformat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",projection=proj)
# I don't know if this imported correctly as you have some duplicate times
SVF <- variogram(DATA,fast=FALSE,dt=c(8,24) %#% 'hr')
ctmm.guess(DATA,variogram=SVF,CTMM=ctmm(error=TRUE)) # tuned tau_velocity=0
FIT <- ctmm.fit(DATA,GUESS)
summary(FIT)
# don't always trust optim when error=TRUE
FIT <- ctmm.fit(DATA,FIT)
summary(FIT)
zoom(SVF,CTMM=FIT) # this looks bad because SVF is mostly errors

# data with errors under 2 km
SVF2 <- variogram(DATA[sqrt(DATA$COV.major)<2000,],fast=FALSE,dt=c(8,24) %#% 'hr')
zoom(SVF2,CTMM=FIT) # this looks better
# all of the data was still used for fitting

UD <- akde(DATA,FIT)
plot(DATA,UD=UD) # I can't see the HR under the telemetry errors
EXT <- extent(UD)
# turning off plot errors and zooming in
plot(DATA,UD=UD,error=FALSE,xlim=EXT$x,ylim=EXT$y)

Just to note, ctmm tries to reduce telemetry error's impact on the home range by smoothing the data before placing the kernels. This contracts the kernels inward, counteracting some of the bias whereby error inflates the home range estimate. This is more than what other people do (nothing), but I'm not sure how ideal it is, statistically speaking.

Best,
Chris
